Subject: Key management & SOC 2 follow-up — Northbridge discovery

Samir / Elena — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

- Redwood status: SOC 2 Type II in progress; last audit window completed May 2027, final report expected Q3 2027. We can share the SOC 2 factsheet and the auditor contact once the report is finalized.
- GDPR/HIPAA: Redwood supports data processing addenda and HIPAA BAAs for Private deployments. For Hosted API, we provide controls and contractual protections; for regulated workloads we recommend Dedicated or Private with customer-managed keys.
- Key management options we discussed (high level):
  * Redwood-managed KMS (default): seamless onboarding, Redwood controls key lifecycle; suitable for non-sensitive workloads.
  * Customer-managed keys (CMK) via cloud KMS (AWS KMS / GCP KMS / Azure Key Vault): customer retains key material control, we integrate key IDs for envelope encryption.
  * HSM-backed BYOK for dedicated/private: FIPS 140-2/3 HSMs and bring-your-own-key with restricted export.

Action items I have for Rishi/Monica to deliver:
1) redwood-kms-diagram.pdf — architecture showing where keys live for each deployment mode (attached).
2) SOC2-compliance-factsheet.pdf — what’s covered and expected delivery window (attached).
3) Northbridge_Security_Questionnaire.xlsx — we started filling high-level answers; Samir, please flag questions you want us to prioritize.

Would you like a short follow-up call next week to walk through the attachments and any additional technical questions (key rotation, HSM attestations, key exportability)? If so, propose 30 minutes — I can include Rishi for pricing/commitment discussion and Monica for the technical deep-dive.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0182

Laura — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifying questions from our security and SRE teams: 

1) For customer-managed keys using AWS KMS, do you require the CMK to be in the same AWS account as our workloads, or can Redwood access a key we grant cross-account permissions to? We need to understand your recommended pattern for least privilege.

2) For HSM/BYOK in Private deployments: can you confirm whether key material ever leaves the HSM? Our procurement requires assurance that private keys are non-exportable.

3) SOC 2: is there an interim report or bridge letter available before the full Type II report is issued? Our compliance deadline is early Q4 and we'd like anything demonstrable sooner.

Also — we've started filling the questionnaire and dropped some comments in rows 12–20 that are high priority. I'll sync with Elena and propose a 30-min slot tomorrow morning (Thu) 09:00–11:00 ET if that works.

Samir — great questions, answers below (high level). Rishi / Monica included for any additional notes and to join the call tomorrow if helpful.

1) AWS KMS pattern: we support both approaches. Recommended for most customers is cross-account CMK with a Grant/Key policy that restricts Redwood's IAM principals to only Encrypt/Decrypt and GenerateDataKey operations for specific key IDs. This preserves key ownership in your account while avoiding the need to host workloads in the same account. We can share a sample IAM policy and KMS key policy. (see redwood-kms-diagram.pdf — section B).

2) HSM/BYOK: for Dedicated and Private we use HSM-backed key stores where key material is non-exportable. Our on-prem and VPC Private deployments can integrate with customer HSMs via PKCS#11 or cloud HSMs; we do not export private key material from a FIPS HSM. We will provide HSM vendor certs/attestations where available.

3) SOC 2 bridge: we can provide our SOC 2 factsheet and a provisional auditor contact. For enterprise customers we can provide a statement of current control coverage and interim audit results under NDA while the final Type II report is issued. If you need a formal bridge letter we can check with our audit team and get back with timing.

Next steps:
- Samir / Elena: confirm if Thu 07:30 or 10:00 ET works (Rishi and Monica can make either).
- Northbridge: please highlight 2–3 questions in the questionnaire you want us to prioritize.

Rishi (pricing): for a BYOK + Private deployment we typically model committed capacity; I’ll let you share the starting estimate surface on the call.

Monica (tech): any additional docs we should surface for key rotation / KMS rotation procedures?

Thanks,
Laura
